subject: Code review: Changes requested for AMSD-2041

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: The `onEntryChange` callback only stores a hash (`ContentstackLivePreview.hash`) in React state — it does NOT re-fetch the changed entry. The prescribed minimal fix explicitly requires: 'In the onEntryChange callback, re-fetch the changed entry using the same Stack ContentType/Entry pattern used by ContentstackFactory.createContentTypeEntryQuery and update React state (useState) that feeds the ContentstackContext.Provider value.' Without re-fetching, draft content is never delivered to `useContent` consumers. The `contentstackContextValue` only carries `livePreviewData` (a hash object) and `setLivePreviewData` — it does not carry updated page/header/footer/onboarding entry data. When the hash changes, `useContent` consumers will re-render (because the context value reference changes), but `getContentByKey` will navigate the same stale data because no entry data was re-fetched. This means none of the acceptance criteria can be met: the Homepage will not show draft entry content, Discover Article pages will not show draft entry content, and successive draft changes will not be reflected.
issues.suggestedFix: In the `onEntryChange` callback, re-fetch the changed entry using the same `getSingleEntry` / `ContentstackFactory.createContentTypeEntryQuery` pattern from `src/services/contentstack.ts`. The callback should receive entry metadata (contentTypeUid, entryUid, lang) from the SDK, use it to re-fetch via `Stack.ContentType(contentTypeUid).Entry(entryUid).language(lang).toJSON().fetch()`, and update React state that carries the actual entry data (not just a hash). The `ContentstackContext.Provider` value must include this re-fetched entry data so that `useContent` consumers receive updated content. Example: `ContentstackLivePreview.onEntryChange((entry) => { // re-fetch entry using Stack, update state with actual entry data })`

issues.description: The `live_preview` config uses `management_token` instead of the prescribed `preview_token`. The Root Cause Analysis explicitly prescribes: `live_preview: { enable: true, preview_token: process.env.CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN || '' }`. The Contentstack Delivery SDK's `live_preview` configuration expects `preview_token` — `management_token` is a Management API credential, not a preview token. The SDK will not recognize `management_token` in the `live_preview` block, so live preview will not be enabled at runtime even though the code compiles. This means the Stack will never return draft entries, and no downstream consumer can receive preview data.
issues.suggestedFix: Change `management_token: CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN` to `preview_token: CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN` in the `live_preview` block. Verify against the installed `contentstack` package's `Config` type definition that `preview_token` is the correct key.

issues.description: Hardcoded endpoint URL `host: "api.contentstack.io"` in the `live_preview` config. Criterion 6 requires no hardcoded strings for endpoint URLs — all must use named constants from `src/config/constants.ts`. The prescribed fix did not mention adding a `host` field at all. If the SDK requires `host`, it should be a named constant; if not, it should be removed.
issues.suggestedFix: Either remove the `host` field (the plan did not prescribe it) or extract it to a named constant in `src/config/constants.ts` (e.g., `CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_HOST`) and reference it there.

issues.description: The `ContentstackContext.Provider` value only carries `livePreviewData` and `setLivePreviewData` — it does not carry the page/header/footer/onboarding entry data that the plan prescribed. The plan states the Provider 'sets the context value from server-side page props (header, footer, onboarding, page)' and the `onEntryChange` callback should 'update React state that feeds the ContentstackContext.Provider value' with re-fetched entry data. The current value object is `{ livePreviewData, setLivePreviewData }` — missing all content fields. Even if page-level components set their own inner Providers, the _app.tsx Provider needs to carry the re-fetched entry data for live preview to work end-to-end.
issues.suggestedFix: Include the re-fetched entry data in the `contentstackContextValue` object. The state should hold actual entry content (page, header, footer, onboarding) that is updated by the `onEntryChange` callback, not just a hash. The Provider value should merge the server-side page props with the live-preview-updated entry data.

issues.description: `ContentstackLivePreview.hash` is accessed without verifying it exists in the SDK's public API. The plan did not mention using a `hash` property. If the installed version of `@contentstack/live-preview-utils` (4.5.0) does not expose `hash` as a public property, this will be `undefined` at runtime.
issues.suggestedFix: Verify `ContentstackLivePreview.hash` exists in the installed package's type definitions. If it does not, remove the hash reference and instead use the entry data provided by the `onEntryChange` callback parameter.

subject: Code review: Changes requested for AMSD-2041

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: The onEntryChange callback hand-rolls ~40 lines of Contentstack query-building logic (ContentType().Entry().language().toJSON(), includeReference, only, except, fetch/findOne, jsonToHTML) that already exists in ContentstackFactory.createContentTypeEntryQuery / createContentTypeQuery and the exported getSingleEntry / getEntry / findSingletonEntry functions in src/services/contentstack.ts. The plan explicitly prescribes: 'The onEntryChange callback in _app.tsx should reuse the same getSingleEntry pattern (via ContentstackFactory.createContentTypeEntryQuery from src/services/contentstack.ts line 185) for client-side re-fetches.' The existing getSingleEntry function handles referenceFieldPath, only, except, jsonRtePath (with renderOption), and error logging — all duplicated here. The fix could be ~5 lines: set the preview hash on Stack.live_preview, then call getSingleEntry or findSingletonEntry.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the hand-rolled query block with: `Stack.live_preview.live_preview = hash; const entry = entryUid ? await getSingleEntry({ contentTypeUid, entryUid, lang, ...contentstackConfig[contentTypeUid] }) : (await getEntry({ contentTypeUid, lang, ...contentstackConfig[contentTypeUid] }))[0];` Import getSingleEntry and getEntry from services/contentstack. This eliminates ~40 lines and fixes the jsonToHTML renderOption inconsistency.

issues.description: The live_preview config uses `management_token` instead of the prescribed `preview_token`. The plan explicitly says: `live_preview: { enable: true, preview_token: process.env.CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN || '' }`. The env var is named CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN (a preview token), but it is assigned to `management_token` (a different token type in the Contentstack SDK). If the SDK does not consume `management_token` in the live_preview config, live preview will silently not work at runtime. The test only verifies the mock was called with the object — it does not verify the SDK actually reads this key.
issues.suggestedFix: Use `preview_token: CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN` as prescribed. If investigation shows the SDK requires `management_token`, document why with a comment and update the plan.

issues.description: Hardcoded `host: 'api.contentstack.io'` in the live_preview config. Review criteria #6 requires all endpoint URLs to use named constants. The existing code already has `CONTENTSTACK_API_HOST` env var used with `Stack.setHost()`. The live_preview host should reuse the same constant or env var, not a string literal.
issues.suggestedFix: Use `host: CONTENTSTACK_API_HOST || 'api.contentstack.io'` or define a named constant in src/constants/contentstack.ts for the preview host.

issues.description: ContentstackLivePreview.init() and onEntryChange() are called inside a useEffect with [locale] dependency. Every locale change re-initializes the live preview utility and registers a new onEntryChange callback without cleaning up the previous one. This can cause: (1) duplicate callbacks firing multiple fetches per entry change, (2) re-initialization side effects (DOM manipulation, internal state reset). The init() should run once on mount; the locale should be captured via a ref so the callback always reads the current value without re-registering.
issues.suggestedFix: Move ContentstackLivePreview.init() to a useEffect([]) (mount-only). Use a `const localeRef = useRef(locale); localeRef.current = locale;` pattern so the onEntryChange callback reads localeRef.current. Register onEntryChange once.

issues.description: jsonToHTML is called without the renderOption parameter that src/services/contentstack.ts uses (line 152: `Utils.jsonToHTML({ entry: result, paths: jsonRtePath, renderOption })`). The renderOption defines span rendering behavior. Omitting it means JSON RTE fields in live preview will render differently from published content, causing visual inconsistency. This would be automatically fixed by reusing getSingleEntry/getEntry (see blocker).
issues.suggestedFix: Pass renderOption (export it from contentstack.ts) or reuse getSingleEntry/getEntry which already includes it.

issues.description: `livePreviewContent?: IContentstackContext | null` is a self-referential type — IContentstackContext contains a field of type IContentstackContext. This is confusing and semantically wrong: livePreviewContent holds partial entry data (e.g., `{ page: [entry] }`), not a full context. It should be `Partial<IContentstackContext>` or a dedicated type.
issues.suggestedFix: Change to `livePreviewContent?: Partial<IContentstackContext> | null` or define a `LivePreviewData` type.

issues.description: `Stack.live_preview as unknown as Record<string, string> & { content_type_uid?: string; entry_uid?: string; }` uses a double cast (`as unknown as`) to bypass TypeScript. This is an untyped escape hatch. The Stack type from the contentstack SDK should be augmented or a proper interface declared for the live_preview shape.
issues.suggestedFix: Declare an interface for the live_preview internal shape and use a single cast, or augment the contentstack module's Stack type.

issues.description: The merge `{ ...content, ...livePreviewContent }` spreads livePreviewContent (which may contain only `{ page: [entry] }`) over content. If livePreviewContent contains `livePreviewContent` itself (from the IContentstackContext type), it would overlay a stale nested value. The type should prevent this, but the self-referential type makes it ambiguous.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a Partial type for livePreviewContent (see minor #1) to make the merge type-safe.
